title: Yara and the Letter
premise: Xanthe Zhou, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made her both brilliant and isolated, receives twin letters after closing a routine claim on a burned warehouse: one confessing to arson and murder, the other promising a second confession if she fails to act. Following clues hidden in a shipping ledger disguised as mundane invoices, she uncovers a protection ring that has quietly destroyed lives in the harbor district for decades—including the fire that orphaned her. As the ring's enforcer closes in, Xanthe must choose between handing her evidence to the corrupt police who shield the ring, or trusting the found family of dockworkers, archivists, and one stubborn retired detective who help her crack the ledger. In the end, she exposes the ring publicly at a hearing, trading her cherished invisibility for justice, and discovers the second letter's author was the sister she never knew she had.
about_author: Coral Ishikawa is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent twelve years reading other people's losses before writing her own stories. She lives in a port city with a rescue dog and an unreasonable collection of antique ledgers.

chapters.title: The Claim That Closed Itself
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She closes the Meridian Warehouse arson claim in record time, filing it as negligence, her photographic memory flagging one invoice that doesn't quite fit. She dismisses the anomaly, as she always does. The emotional beat is professional satisfaction shadowed by a flicker of unease she can't name.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Two letters arrive the same morning: one confessing to the warehouse fire and a murder ten years old, the other promising a second confession 'when you understand the first.' No return address, handwriting she almost recognizes. The emotional beat is the crack in her controlled world.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with flashback. We learn why she never takes sides: a childhood spent erased in the foster system, memory as both gift and burden. She decides to investigate privately, telling no one. The emotional beat is loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She returns to the claim file and realizes the 'mundane' invoices form a coded ledger—payments routed through the harbor authority. Her memory reconstructs the pattern instantly, but decoding it requires records she can't legally access. The emotional beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Detective Off the Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: retired detective Marisol Vega, who worked the decade-old murder and was forced out for asking questions. She recognizes the confession letter's phrasing. She begins her own quiet inquiry, unaware Xanthe is on the same trail. The emotional beat is old guilt rekindled.

chapters.title: The Dockworkers' Table
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Her ledger trail leads to a dockside diner where longshoremen share an unspoken code of silence—and protection. She's warned off by a foreman named Odile, but notices the diner functions as a family for people the system discarded. The emotional beat is longing for belonging she won't admit.

chapters.title: Second Fire
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A records annex burns overnight, destroying exactly the files Marisol had requested. The message is clear: someone is watching the watchers. Xanthe realizes her letters' author predicted this. The emotional beat is escalating fear and the first proof the conspiracy is alive.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, flashback-heavy. A memory surfaces: the harbor fire from her childhood, a woman's voice, a ledger page burning. She realizes the decade-old murder victim may be connected to her own past. The emotional beat is grief breaking through professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Enforcer
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A man named Calloway, the ring's fixer, is assigned to identify who pulled the ledger thread. His methodical menace contrasts with Xanthe's precision. He visits her office under a false pretext; she clocks the lie instantly but lets him leave. The emotional beat is a duel of masks.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Odile catches Xanthe photographing harbor manifests and, instead of turning her in, reveals the dockworkers have protected the ledger's secret for years to keep their jobs—and their lives. She offers Xanthe a choice: stop, or become one of them. The emotional beat is the first real offer of trust.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. As promised, a second letter arrives—confessing to the murder, and naming the writer as someone inside the ring who wants out. The handwriting finally resolves in Xanthe's memory: it matches a name in her own childhood file. The emotional beat is vertigo—personal and professional cases collapsing into one.

chapters.title: Marisol's Mistake
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She confronts an old informant directly and is seen doing it. Calloway now has two threads to pull. Marisol, realizing she's endangered Xanthe, tracks her down through the insurance company. The emotional beat is guilt forcing a proud woman to ask for help.

chapters.title: Two Investigators, One Table
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Xanthe and Marisol compare notes at the dockworkers' diner, reconstructing the ring's structure: a harbor commissioner, an insurer's executive, and Calloway's muscle. Xanthe's memory supplies the ledger key; Marisol supplies the names. The emotional beat is cautious partnership becoming genuine kinship.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the ledger's final cipher, they find a hidden archive beneath the harbor authority—decades of payoffs, including a file on the fire that killed Xanthe's mother. The letter writer's name appears throughout: R. Zhou. The emotional beat is devastating recognition.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Diner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Calloway raids the diner network; someone talked. Odile is taken in for questioning, and the found family fractures under fear. Xanthe must decide whether to trade the archive's location for Odile's release. The emotional beat is loyalty tested at real cost.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She weighs handing everything to the police—knowing the commissioner controls them—against going public with no legal protection. Marisol argues for the law; Odile, released but broken, argues for the truth at any price. The emotional beat is the theme made explicit: love against duty, justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax setup. She sets a trap using the ledger's own code, publishing a decoy page only the ring would react to. The response comes from R. Zhou—Ren, her sister, a clerk inside the harbor authority who has been feeding the letters to force the truth out. The emotional beat is reunion shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Calloway Closes In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Calloway traces Ren, and the sisters are cornered in the archive as Calloway arrives to burn it—and them—with it. Marisol and the dockworkers, tipped by Odile, converge. The emotional beat is terror transformed into defiance.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. Rather than run, Xanthe walks the evidence into a public insurance fraud hearing, reciting the ledger from memory before cameras while Ren's documents corroborate every figure. Calloway is arrested attempting to silence her in the hallway; the commissioner resigns under the lights. The emotional beat is invisibility traded, deliberately, for justice.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The fallout: indictments, the dockworkers' union reclaiming the diner, Marisol offered her badge back and declining. She and Xanthe visit the graves Xanthe never knew she had. The emotional beat is mourning that finally has somewhere to go.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Three
chapters.summary: Ren's POV. The sisters navigate the awkward, tender work of becoming family—shared mannerisms, shared grief, a mother's recipes. Odile offers Ren a place at the dockworkers' table, and by extension, Xanthe. The emotional beat is belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Case She Keeps
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Months later, a new letter arrives on her desk—an ordinary claim with an anomaly only she would notice. She smiles, keeps it, and for the first time answers the door when help is offered. The emotional beat is the investigator who once stayed invisible, now unmistakably seen.
